HasUponPickupEffect.rationale: PandorasBox.cs:19 `HasUponPickupEffect => true`; the flag feeds RelicModel.IsTradable, mirrored at relics/base.py:126-136. Matches.

AfterObtained.rationale: PandorasBox.cs:21-30. TARGET SET: `c != null && c.IsBasicStrikeOrDefend && c.IsRemovable`. IsBasicStrikeOrDefend is `Rarity == CardRarity.Basic && (Tags.Contains(Strike) || Tags.Contains(Defend))` (CardModel.cs:677-694) and it is `virtual` with ZERO overrides anywhere in the game (executed grep), so pandoras_box.py:22-26's `c.rarity == CardRarity.BASIC and ("strike" in c.tags or "defend" in c.tags)` over `run.removable_cards()` (IsRemovable = not Eternal, run.py:360-362) is the same set. REPLACEMENTS: `CardFactory.CreateRandomCardForTransform(c, isInCombat: false, base.Owner.RunState.Rng.Niche)` per card, and run.transform_card(card, pick_rng=niche) is the sim's equivalent with the same stream (see N1). ORDER: C#'s `Select` is lazy but `CardCmd.Transform` forces it with `transformations.ToArray()` (CardCmd.cs:375) before removing anything, then sorts the appends by the originals' pile index (PileIndexSort, CardCmd.cs:353-360, :405) -- for a single Deck pile that is ascending deck order, which is also the order the sim's loop rolls and appends in. The rolls are order-independent anyway: GetFilteredTransformationOptions depends only on the ORIGINAL card's rarity and id (CardFactory.cs:189-212), never on the current deck, so rolling all five up front and rolling them one at a time consume the Niche stream identically. Line 26-28's NSimpleCardsViewScreen is presentation.

guards.what: N1 (PROMPT.md bug class 16): C# names `RunState.Rng.Niche` explicitly (PandorasBox.cs:24) and the sim DOES pass it
guards.rationale: pandoras_box.py:30 is `niche = run.rng_set.niche if run.rng_set is not None else None`, and run.transform_card's `pick_rng` parameter is documented as exactly this argument, naming Pandora's Box as the caller (run.py:430-435). Checked because this is the failure mode class 16 warns about and audit/records/relic/astrolabe.json N1 filed as a live gap for the same helper: there the port left pick_rng at its None default and silently fell back to the legacy shared random.Random. Here it does not. The stream is genuinely CONSUMED rather than merely named -- CreateRandomCardForTransform calls `rng.NextItem(...)` directly (CardFactory.cs:177-181), unlike the `claws` case class 16 cites where an explicit Replacement means GetReplacement never touches the Rng. The `else None` branch is the legacy RL path, the repo-wide convention for runs with no rng_set.

guards.what: N2 (PROMPT.md bug class 8): deck placement -- an out-of-combat transform APPENDS at the deck's end rather than replacing in place
guards.rationale: run.transform_card's docstring records the rule and cites CardCmd.cs:437, and names Pandora's Box as the reason it matters ('appends its 8 rolls after the deck's existing cards') because the combat-start UnstableShuffle is order-dependent. Verified against CardCmd.Transform itself: the originals are all removed first (CardCmd.cs:402) and the replacements added afterwards in PileIndexSort order (:405-407). NOTE per binding rule 7: this leans on sts2_rl/run.py, which this record does NOT hash.

guards.what: N3: the replacements are not upgraded, and a transformed card can roll into any Common/Uncommon/Rare of the same pool except itself
guards.rationale: GetFilteredTransformationOptions keeps only rarities 2-4 (Common/Uncommon/Rare) for a non-Curse original, excludes `c.Id == original.Id`, and applies FilterForPlayerCount (CardFactory.cs:189-212); `isInCombat: false` means the CanBeGeneratedInCombat filter is NOT applied, so out-of-run cards stay offerable -- the same reading audit/records/relic/burning_sticks.json records for the reward pool (binding rule 3). run.transform_card's docstring states the same rules for the deck-level path. The port's docstring statement 'Replacements are not upgraded' is correct: CreateCard produces a level-0 card and nothing upgrades it.
